name: enhanced for-each traversal of the list vs. index-based loop with get()/[] access
side_a: No deduct when the response traverses the ArrayList with an enhanced for loop (`for (CourseRecord cr : historyList)`), since the construct itself guarantees every element of the list is reached and no index/bounds expression can go wrong.
side_b: Deduct when the response uses an index-based loop to reach elements and any part of that indexing apparatus is wrong (bound taken from the wrong list, array `[]` subscripting, `.length` on an ArrayList), because then the response has not demonstrated correct access to every element.

name: loop bound matches the list being indexed vs. bound taken from a different list
side_a: No deduct when the traversal's extent is governed by the very list whose elements are being accessed, so all of its elements are covered.
side_b: Deduct when the loop bound comes from a different ArrayList than the one being indexed (e.g., `i < mathList.size()` controlling `historyList.get(i)`), since this neither visits all of historyList's elements nor guarantees a legal index.

name: Direct public-field access on CourseRecord vs. actual accessor method invocation
side_a: No_deduct when the response retrieves the ID and absence data by actually invoking the accessor methods on a CourseRecord element (e.g., hist.getStudentID(), math.getAbsences()), regardless of loop style, comparison operator (== vs .equals), or logical errors elsewhere.
side_b: Deduct when the response reads the data via direct instance-field/attribute access instead of a method call (e.g., historyList[i].studentID, mathList[j].absences); bare field references are not credited as calls to getStudentID/getAbsences even though the intent and the receiver type are clear.

name: the comparison must read absence values vs. identifying matching students suffices
side_a: deduct unless the method actually retrieves and compares the `absences` fields of CourseRecord objects; code that only matches student IDs and increments a counter (never calling getAbsences) earns no credit for this item, since the required comparison is absent entirely.
side_b: no_deduct if the method correctly identifies the students common to both lists and produces a count from them, treating the ID-matching/count structure as satisfying the comparison sub-item even though absence values are never accessed.

name: operator must be strictly greater-than vs. any ordering comparison of absences counts
side_a: deduct if the only absences comparison in the response uses a non-strict operator (>=, <=), because counting students with equal absences does not establish that one has MORE absences than the other.
side_b: no_deduct if the response compares the two absence values with any ordering operator (including >=), on the grounds that it still shows the intended 'history vs. math absences' comparison and only the boundary case is wrong.

name: Student-ID matching: .equals()/collection-based string comparison vs == reference comparison
side_a: If the answer matches records by comparing student IDs with .equals() (or an equivalent String-aware collection lookup), the matching step counts as correct — no deduction.
side_b: If the answer matches records by comparing the String student IDs with ==, the match is not reliably performed — deduct.

name: Absence counts actually compared vs only ID membership counted
side_a: If the answer retrieves and compares the two absence values for the matched student before incrementing the counter, credit.
side_b: If the answer only checks that the student appears in both lists and increments without ever reading/comparing absences, deduct.
